yao.en: I'd really like to work in Beijing.
yao.why: A wish takes 想, and only 想 can have 很 in front.
Ordering what you've decided on: 要 + the thing.

yao.ch: 我想去中国旅游，但是没有时间。
yao.en: I'd like to travel to China, but I don't have time.
yao.why: It's only a wish, not settled, so 想 fits.

yao.en: The doctor says I need to rest more.
yao.why: Something you must do takes 要; 想 is only a wish.

yao.en: I'm not feeling well - I need to go to the hospital.
yao.why: 要 comes right before the verb for something you must do.

zai.en: My dad works at a company.
zai.why: 在 + place comes before the verb.

zai.en: My older brother works near the airport.
zai.why: 在 + place goes before the verb, not after it.

zai.en: Don't talk - the child is sleeping.
zai.why: 在 right before a verb means it's happening now.
The place goes before the verb: 在 + place + verb.

zai.en: Wait a moment - Mum's on the phone.
zai.why: 在 directly before the verb means it's in progress.

keneng.en: He didn't come today - he might be ill.
keneng.why: A guess about why takes 可能; 能 and 可以 are about being able or allowed.

keneng.en: He's not home - he's probably gone to the shop.
keneng.why: 可能 goes right before the verb 去.

keneng.ch: 我的手机可能在教室里。
keneng.en: My phone might be in the classroom.
keneng.why: 可能 before 在 turns it into a guess.
Asking if someone is able takes 能; 可能 is only a guess.

keneng.en: That man might be her husband.
keneng.why: 可能 goes before the verb 是.

verb-redup.ch: 走了一个小时了，我们__吧。
verb-redup.en: We've been walking for an hour - let's take a little rest.
verb-redup.why: A two-syllable verb doubles as a whole: 休息休息.

verb-redup.en: Let's go out for a little walk.
verb-redup.why: 走走 is 走 said twice: a short, easy walk. It comes after 出去.

verb-redup.en: Think it over, then tell me.
verb-redup.why: A one-syllable verb can double with 一 in the middle: 想一想.

verb-redup.en: Let's get a bit of exercise together.
verb-redup.why: Two-syllable verbs repeat as ABAB, not AABB.

verb-redup.en: This book is great - you should have a look too.
verb-redup.why: 看看 is the verb here; doubling it makes a light suggestion.

rang-jiao.en: Mum doesn't let me go out alone at night.
rang-jiao.why: To say someone won't let you, 不 goes before 让.

rang-jiao.en: His mum doesn't let him play on his phone.
rang-jiao.why: 不 goes before 让, not before the second verb.

rang-jiao.ch: 老师叫我们明天早上八点到教室。
rang-jiao.en: The teacher told us to be in the classroom at eight tomorrow morning.
rang-jiao.why: 叫 works like 让: teacher + 叫 + us + what we do.

rang-jiao.en: My friend asked me to go to the airport.
rang-jiao.why: The person comes right after 让, then what they do.

rang-jiao.en: The doctor told him to drink more water and less coffee.
rang-jiao.why: A 让 B + verb: 让 sits between the doctor and him.

zhe.en: The children came into the classroom laughing.
zhe.why: Verb + 着 before a second verb says how that action was done.
坐着 is the state she's in; the second verb 看 follows it.

zhe.ch: 她穿着新衣服去上班了。
zhe.en: She went to work in her new clothes.
zhe.why: 穿着 describes what she had on while she went.
The negative of verb + 着 uses 没有, not 不.

zhe.en: The child just looked at Mum and said nothing.
zhe.why: 着 goes right after the verb 看: he kept looking.

guo.en: I've never been to China - I'd really like to go.
guo.why: Never having done it is 没有 + verb + 过.
The negative is 没有 + verb + 过; 过 stays after the verb.

guo.ch: 他坐过飞机，我没有坐过。
guo.en: He's been on a plane; I haven't.
guo.why: 过 marks experience, and it stays in the negative: 没有坐过.
过 goes right after the verb, before the place.

guo.en: I've read this book - it's really interesting.
guo.why: 过 goes straight after the verb 看.

yao-le.ch: 下个星期__考试了，我要准备一下。
yao-le.en: The exam is next week - I need to get ready.
yao-le.why: With a time word like 下个星期, use 就要, not 快要.

yao-le.en: The plane is about to reach Beijing.
yao-le.why: 快要 goes before the verb, and 了 closes the sentence.

yao-le.ch: 我们快要到了，你等我一下。
yao-le.en: We're nearly there - wait for me a moment.
yao-le.why: 快要……了 says it will happen very soon.

yao-le.en: My little sister will soon be eighteen.
yao-le.why: 要……了 needs 了 at the end.

yao-le.en: It's getting dark - let's go home.
yao-le.why: 要 goes before 黑 and 了 ends it: about to happen.

yijing.en: Don't wait for him - he's already left.
yijing.why: 已经 + verb + 了: it has already happened.

yijing.en: They've already got to the airport.
yijing.why: 已经 comes before the verb, and 了 comes at the end.
已经 works with ages too, and still ends with 了.
已经 nearly always has 了 at the end.

yijing.en: You can stop - I already know.
yijing.why: 已经 goes right before the verb 知道.

result.ch: 老师说得太快了，我没有听__。
result.en: The teacher spoke too fast - I didn't understand.
result.why: 懂 after 听 says whether you understood; 没有 negates it.
错 goes straight after the verb 说: the result was wrong.

result.ch: 你等我一下，我还没有吃完。
result.en: Wait for me - I haven't finished eating.
result.why: 没有 + verb + result: 吃完 hasn't happened yet.
The result word sits right after the verb; 了 comes after it.

result.en: I'll finish this question, then go and play.
result.why: 完 goes straight after the verb 做: finished.

de-degree.en: You write too fast - I can't read it.
de-degree.why: 得 after the verb 写 brings in how it's done.
With an object, say the verb again before 得: 做菜做得……

de-degree.en: Did you have a good time?
de-degree.why: 得 + adjective describes how the playing went.
With an object, repeat the verb before 得.
The negative goes after 得: 写得不太好.

ci.en: He's been to China three times.
ci.why: Number + 次 counts the times; 第 would give the order instead.
一次 goes after the verb 写.

ci.ch: 我们一个星期上两次课。
ci.en: We have class twice a week.
ci.why: 两次 comes after the verb 上, before the object 课.

ci.en: I've been to his place once.
ci.why: The number and 次 go after the verb, not before it.

ci.en: How many times have you been to Beijing?
ci.why: 次 follows the number 几, right after the verb.

de-phrase.en: This one's too small - do you have a bigger one?
de-phrase.why: 大的 = a big one; the noun is left out after 的.

de-phrase.en: I want to buy a new one.
de-phrase.why: 一个新的 = a new one; 的 stands in for the noun.

de-phrase.ch: 这不是我的手机，我的是白的。
de-phrase.en: This isn't my phone - mine is white.
de-phrase.why: 我的 and 白的 both leave the noun 手机 out.

de-phrase.en: Of these apples, I want the big ones.
de-phrase.why: To pick one, keep 的 after the describer: 大的.

de-phrase.en: This top is my little sister's.
de-phrase.why: 我妹妹的 = my sister's; the noun 衣服 is left out.

verb-attr.ch: 你昨天看__电影叫什么名字？
verb-attr.en: What's the name of the film you saw yesterday?
verb-attr.why: 你昨天看 + 的 describes the film: the film you saw.

verb-attr.en: The food my mum makes is really good.
verb-attr.why: The description 我妈妈做 comes before 的 and the noun 菜.

verb-attr.ch: 坐在我旁边的人是我的同学。
verb-attr.en: The person sitting next to me is my classmate.
verb-attr.why: The whole description 坐在我旁边 goes before 的人.

verb-attr.en: The people in white are doctors.
verb-attr.why: The description goes before the noun: 穿白衣服的人.
你说 + 的 goes in front of the noun to say which restaurant.

bi.en: This phone is more expensive than that one.
bi.why: After 比 the adjective stands alone - no 很, 非常 or 真.

bi.en: This top is prettier than that one.
bi.why: A + 比 B + adjective: the adjective comes last, on its own.

bi.ch: 这儿的水果比商店的便宜。
bi.en: The fruit here is cheaper than in the shops.
bi.why: A 比 B + 便宜, with nothing before the adjective.
比 already means "more", so drop 很.

bi.en: Today's watermelon tastes better than yesterday's.
bi.why: 比 goes between the two things being compared.

bi-more.ch: 这件比那件贵__，我买那件吧。
bi-more.en: This one's a bit more expensive than that one - I'll get that one.
bi-more.why: The gap goes after the adjective: 贵一点儿.

bi-more.en: My older sister is five years older than me.
bi-more.why: The exact amount goes after the adjective: 大五岁.

bi-more.en: My place is much farther away than his.
bi-more.why: 多了 after the adjective means "much more".

bi-more.ch: 这个苹果比那个一点儿大。
bi-more.fix: 这个苹果比那个大一点儿。
bi-more.en: This apple is a little bigger than that one.
bi-more.why: 一点儿 goes after the adjective, not before it.

bi-more.en: This room is much bigger than that one.
bi-more.why: 多了 comes after the adjective to say "much".

yinwei.ch: 因为今天是星期天，__商店里人很多。
yinwei.en: It's Sunday, so the shops are busy.
yinwei.why: 因为 gives the reason; 所以 brings in the result.

yinwei.en: I was too tired, so I didn't go running.
yinwei.why: The reason with 因为 comes first, the result with 所以 second.

yinwei.ch: 我没有买那件衣服，因为太贵了。
yinwei.en: I didn't buy that top because it was too expensive.
yinwei.why: 因为 can come second, to give the reason afterwards.

yinwei.ch: 因为他很忙，但是没有时间休息。
yinwei.fix: 因为他很忙，所以没有时间休息。
yinwei.en: He's very busy, so he has no time to rest.
yinwei.why: 因为 pairs with 所以, not 但是.

yinwei.en: It's a long way, so we're taking a taxi.
yinwei.why: 所以 opens the result half, after the reason.

suiran.en: I'm tired, but I'm very happy.
suiran.why: 虽然 pairs with 但是 for a contrast; 所以 would give a result.

suiran.en: He's ill, but he still went to work.
suiran.why: 虽然 opens the fact, 但是 opens the contrast.

suiran.ch: 这个房间虽然很小，但是很便宜。
suiran.en: This room is small, but it's cheap.
suiran.why: 虽然 can come after the subject; 但是 still opens the second half.

suiran.ch: 虽然我不太会说汉语，我能听懂。
suiran.fix: 虽然我不太会说汉语，但是我能听懂。
suiran.en: I can't really speak Chinese, but I can understand it.
suiran.why: Keep 但是 in the second half.

suiran.en: This restaurant isn't big, but the food is great.
suiran.why: 虽然 goes before the first fact; 但是 brings the contrast.

li.en: My home isn't very far from the airport.
li.why: 离 measures the distance between two places; 从 is where you start from.

li.en: There are three days to go until the exam.
li.why: 离 can measure time too: from now until the exam.

li.ch: 他家离这儿不太远，走路十分钟。
li.en: His place isn't far from here - ten minutes on foot.
li.why: A 离 B + 远 / 近 gives the distance between them.

li.en: The station is close to the hotel.
li.why: For distance use 离; 从 marks where a trip starts.

li.en: The shop is close to my home - I go every day.
li.why: 离 sits between the two places: 商店离我家.

prep.en: Drinking more water is good for you.
prep.why: 对 + thing: what it is good for.

prep.en: He's gone home from the office.
prep.why: 从 + place goes before the verb.
对 + person comes before the adjective.
往 + direction goes before the verb, not after it.

prep.en: I'm coming back from Beijing tomorrow.
prep.why: 从 + place sits before the verb 回来.

di.en: This is my third time in Beijing.
di.why: 第 before the number gives the order: the third time.

di.en: This is my second time on a plane.
di.why: 第 goes right before the number: 第二次 = the second time.

di.ch: 我们家有三个孩子，我是第二个。
di.en: There are three kids in our family - I'm the second.
di.why: 第二个 = the second one; 三个 just counts.

di.ch: 今天是我们上课的二天。
di.fix: 今天是我们上课的第二天。
di.en: Today is our second day of class.
di.why: An order needs 第: 第二天 = the second day.

di.en: The third person from the right is my older brother.
di.why: 第 goes before the number to give the order.

zui.ch: 我们家四个人里，我妹妹__小。
zui.en: Of the four of us at home, my little sister is the youngest.
zui.why: 最 + adjective ranks her above everyone: the youngest.
最 goes right before the adjective 好.

zui.ch: 这件衣服最便宜，我买这件。
zui.en: This top is the cheapest - I'll buy it.
zui.why: 最 + adjective: the cheapest of them all.
最 goes before 喜欢, never after it.

zui.en: Which dish do you think tastes best?
zui.why: 最 goes right before the adjective 好吃.

zhen.why: Inside a description before a noun use 很; 真 is only for exclaiming.
真 goes right before the adjective to exclaim.
真 + adjective is a heartfelt exclamation.
真 goes before the adjective, not after it.
真 goes right before the adjective 好.

jiu.ch: 他七点__到公司了，大家都还没有来。
jiu.en: He got to the office as early as seven - nobody else was there yet.
jiu.why: Time + 就 + verb + 了: earlier than you'd think.

jiu.en: His home is right next to the school.
jiu.why: 就 before 在 means "right there".

jiu.en: I'll come and find you as soon as I've eaten.
jiu.why: 就 says the next thing happens right away.

jiu.ch: 我昨天晚上九点就睡觉。
jiu.fix: 我昨天晚上九点就睡觉了。
jiu.en: Last night I went to bed as early as nine.
jiu.why: About the past, 就 usually needs 了 at the end.

jiu.en: He could swim by the age of six.
jiu.why: 就 comes after the time 六岁: earlier than you'd expect.

hai.ch: 已经十二点了，他__在工作。
hai.en: It's already twelve and he's still working.
hai.why: 还 + 在 + verb: it's still going on.
还没有 + verb = not yet; 还 comes first.

hai.ch: 这个很好吃，我还想要一个。
hai.en: This is delicious - I'd like another one.
hai.why: 还 before 想 means one more.
还 goes before 在, not after it.
还 before 要 asks about something more.

zai-again.ch: 我今天没有时间，我们明天__说吧。
zai-again.en: I don't have time today - let's talk tomorrow.
zai-again.why: 再 points forward: do it later, not now.

zai-again.en: This one's a bit pricey - I'll look around a bit more.
zai-again.why: 再 goes before the verb: look more, later.

zai-again.ch: 请你明天再给我打电话。
zai-again.why: 再 is for a repeat that hasn't happened yet.

zai-again.en: Could you say that once more?
zai-again.why: 再 goes before the verb, not after it.

zai-again.en: I'll come and see you again tomorrow.
zai-again.why: 再 goes before the verb and points to the future.

youdianr.ch: 今天__冷，你多穿一件衣服吧。
youdianr.en: It's a bit cold today - put on another layer.
youdianr.why: 有点儿 goes before the adjective: a bit too cold for comfort.

youdianr.en: It's a bit far - let's take a taxi.
youdianr.why: 有点儿 sits before the adjective 远.
有点儿 can go before 不 + adjective too.

youdianr.en: This phone is a bit expensive.
youdianr.why: Before an adjective use 有点儿; 一点儿 goes after it.

youdianr.en: I'm a bit busy today - let's go tomorrow.
youdianr.why: 有点儿 goes right before the adjective 忙.

mei.why: Time words like 天 take 每 directly - no 个.

mei.en: Each of us has a copy.
mei.why: 每个人 is followed by 都 before the verb.

mei.en: He travels to China every year.
mei.why: 每年 needs no measure word, and 都 comes before the verb.

mei.fix: 每个孩子都喜欢吃西瓜。
mei.why: 每 almost always needs 都 before the verb.

mei.en: He calls his mum every week.
mei.why: 每 comes before the measure word 个.
ppy: dōu gěi mā ma dǎ diàn huà

shibushi.en: You didn't come yesterday - were you ill?
shibushi.why: 是不是 before the part you're checking asks someone to confirm a guess.

shibushi.en: This top is a bit big, isn't it?
shibushi.why: 是不是 can go at the end to check a guess.
是不是 goes before the part being checked.
是不是 already makes a question - drop 吗.

shibushi.en: You can't find your phone, is that it?
shibushi.why: 是不是 goes before the part you're checking: 找不到.

duo-adj.why: 多 + adjective asks for a measurement; 多少 asks how many.
有 + 多 + adjective asks for a measurement.

duo-adj.en: How old is your little sister now?

duo-adj.why: For a measurement use 多 + adjective; 多少 counts things.

duo-adj.en: How tall do you think he is?
duo-adj.why: 多 goes right before the adjective 高.

haoma.en: Get me a watermelon, will you?
haoma.why: Add 好吗 after a request to ask the other person to agree.
The request comes first; 好吗 goes at the end.

haoma.ch: 我们下午一起去商店，好吗？
haoma.en: Let's go to the shop together this afternoon, OK?
haoma.why: 好吗 after a suggestion asks the other person to agree.
好吗 goes after the request, not in front of it.

haoma.en: Wait five minutes for me, OK?

bushi-ma.ch: 你__喜欢喝咖啡吗？今天怎么喝茶了？
bushi-ma.en: I thought you liked coffee - how come you're having tea today?
bushi-ma.why: 不是……吗 means you believed it and something doesn't fit.

bushi-ma.en: Isn't this the book you wanted?
bushi-ma.why: 不是 goes right after the subject and 吗 closes it: you're pointing out what should be obvious.

bushi-ma.ch: 你不是在北京工作吗？怎么在这儿？
bushi-ma.en: Don't you work in Beijing? What are you doing here?
bushi-ma.why: 不是……吗: you thought so, and seeing him here doesn't fit.
不是……吗 needs 吗 at the end.
不是 goes right after the subject; 吗 ends the sentence.

zenme-why.en: How come you're not eating? This is delicious.
zenme-why.why: 怎么 before 不 + verb asks "how come", with surprise.

zenme-why.ch: 他今天__没有来上课？是不是生病了？
zenme-why.en: How come he didn't come to class today? Is he ill?
zenme-why.why: 怎么 + 没有 + verb asks why it didn't happen.

zenme-why.en: How come you're here on your own?
zenme-why.why: 怎么 before the verb asks "how come", not "how".

zenme-why.en: How come he isn't saying anything?
zenme-why.why: To ask "how come", use 怎么 alone; 怎么样 asks "how is it".

zenme-why.en: How did you know I was here?
zenme-why.why: 怎么 goes right before the verb 知道.

yixia.en: Come here a moment - how do you read this character?
yixia.why: Verb + 一下 makes it a quick, light request.
一下 goes right after the verb 休息.

yixia.ch: 我想问一下，火车站在哪儿？
yixia.en: Can I just ask - where's the railway station?
yixia.why: 问一下 softens the question: just a quick ask.

yixia.en: Take a quick look at this book.
yixia.why: 一下 comes after the verb, not before it.

yixia.en: Get yourself ready - we're leaving at nine.
yixia.why: 一下 goes right after the verb 准备.

bie.why: An order uses 别; plain 不 can't tell someone not to.

bie.en: Stop playing on the computer and take a break.
bie.why: 别 + verb + 了 = stop doing it.
不要 + verb works like 别: don't.
Plain 不 can't give an order; use 别.

bie.en: You've got an exam tomorrow - stop playing.
bie.why: 别 goes right before the verb: 别玩了 = stop playing.

deshihou.en: When I got home, it was already twelve.
deshihou.why: 的时候 goes at the end of the "when" part.

deshihou.en: When he came, I was asleep.
deshihou.why: 的时候 closes the "when" part, which comes before the main sentence.

deshihou.ch: 下雨的时候，我喜欢在家看书。
deshihou.en: When it rains, I like to stay in and read.
deshihou.why: 下雨的时候 sets the time before the main sentence.

deshihou.ch: 的时候我在北京，认识了他。
deshihou.fix: 我在北京的时候，认识了他。
deshihou.en: I met him when I was in Beijing.
deshihou.why: 的时候 comes at the end of the "when" part, not the start.

deshihou.en: Call me when you get to the airport.
deshihou.why: 的时候 goes right after 你到机场, the "when" part.

approx.ch: 从这儿到机场要一个__小时。
approx.en: It takes over an hour from here to the airport.
approx.why: With numbers under ten, 多 goes after the measure word: 一个多小时.

approx.en: There are twenty-odd students in the classroom.
approx.why: 多 goes straight after a round number, before the measure word.

approx.ch: 这件衣服一百多块，不贵。
approx.en: This top is just over a hundred yuan - not expensive.
approx.why: Round number + 多 + measure word: a bit over a hundred.

approx.en: There are a dozen or so people in our company.
approx.why: 几 goes right after 十, before the measure word.
多 after the round number 三十 means "over thirty".

mw-redup.en: Every one of these classmates can speak Chinese.
mw-redup.why: 个个 = every single one, and 都 follows it.

mw-redup.en: Every one of them can swim.
mw-redup.why: 个个 sits at the front, before 都.

mw-redup.ch: 我妈妈天天都给我打电话。
mw-redup.en: My mum calls me every single day.
mw-redup.why: 天天 = every day, and 都 comes before the verb.
天天 goes at the front as the time, not after the verb.

mw-redup.en: Every single one of my classmates likes this teacher.
mw-redup.why: 个个 follows the people it covers and comes before 都.

er-liang.en: There are two of us at home, Dad and me.
er-liang.why: 口 is a measure word, so two is 两.

er-liang.en: Today is the first of February.
er-liang.why: A month is a number read out: 二月.
The hour counts with 点, a measure word: 两点.

er-liang.en: I'd like two cups of coffee.
er-liang.why: 杯 is a measure word, so it takes 两.
Inside a bigger number, two stays 二.

hui-neng-keyi.en: Can you drive? I learned last year.
hui-neng-keyi.why: Driving is a skill you learn: 会.

hui-neng-keyi.ch: 对不起，我明天有事，不__来了。
hui-neng-keyi.en: Sorry, something has come up tomorrow and I can't come.
hui-neng-keyi.why: It is about being able to, this time: 能.
Asking to be allowed: 可以.

hui-neng-keyi.ch: 我能说汉语，我学了两年了。
hui-neng-keyi.fix: 我会说汉语，我学了两年了。
hui-neng-keyi.en: I can speak Chinese; I've been learning for two years.
hui-neng-keyi.why: A skill you learned takes 会.
Not allowed: 不可以. 不能 would be fine too.
